I've updated `0.svg`. It was an empty `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"/>` element, which displays as a blank 300×150 box. The filename was the only hint, so I made it a clean "0" icon:

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" role="img">
  <title>Zero</title>
  <path d="M12 3C16 3 18 6 18 12S16 21 12 21S6 18 6 12S8 3 12 3Z"/>
</svg>
```

- **Scales cleanly:** it now has a `viewBox` and a 24px default size, which is the standard icon grid. It resizes without blurring and won't stretch to fill its container.
- **Looks like a number, not the letter O:** the shape is a tall oval with slightly straighter sides than a plain ellipse, like a "0" in a sans-serif font. Every coordinate is a whole number, so the 2px stroke stays sharp at 24px.
- **Matches the text color:** `currentColor` makes it take the surrounding text color when placed directly in HTML. Used as an image, it shows in black.
- **Accessible:** `role="img"` and `<title>` give screen readers the name "Zero." The title also appears as the browser tab title when the file is opened directly.

**I couldn't validate or render it.** `xmllint` and Quick Look both needed permission, and nobody can approve prompts in this session. I checked the markup and the curve maths by hand, but I haven't seen it rendered, so it's worth opening in a browser to look. No preview files were created, so there's nothing to clean up.
